title: Let’s Worm
summary: A literary-art collaboration with more than 100 works—and a curated digital home built for its stories, illustrations, and worms.
intro: Since 2017, writer Dan Murphy and I have prompted one another through stories and images; the current site gives a selected part of that long-running exchange its own editorial identity.

heroImage.alt: Let’s Worm issue landing page featuring the Moon City title and a large sculptural pink worm

role: Illustration · Editorial collaboration · Web design and engineering

designSystem.name: Let's Worm Design System
designSystem.summary: A warm, strange, and accessible editorial system that gives Let's Worm a coherent literary identity while keeping stories resilient across themes, viewports, content lengths, and input methods.

principles.name: Editorial before ornamental
principles.description: Stories, contributors, and issue context remain clear before the system introduces visual flourish.

principles.name: Warm, strange, and human
principles.description: Caslon, Futura, paper tones, mauve, and the worm motif create handmade character without compromising legibility.

principles.name: Movement has meaning
principles.description: Motion communicates state and continuity while reduced-motion users receive an equivalent static experience.

principles.name: Resilient by default
principles.description: Components tolerate long titles, absent images, narrow containers, zoom, and light or dark environments.

principles.name: Native interaction first
principles.description: Links, buttons, forms, headings, and landmarks retain native behavior, visible focus, and clear accessible names.

typography.description: Carries stories and long-form editorial content with a literary voice.
Marks structure, navigation, metadata, and expressive headlines.
Supports code-like and technical moments without entering story text.

components.name: Actions
components.description: Native buttons share one action and focus language across editorial and utility flows.

components.name: Field guidance and error
components.description: Visible labels, associated guidance, and errors keep forms understandable in every state.

components.name: Empty state
components.description: A quiet editorial fallback explains the absence of stories without turning the page into a dead end.

componentSnapshot.alt: Let’s Worm design-system specimens showing action states, invalid field guidance, and an empty editorial state
componentSnapshot.caption: Actions, field feedback, and the empty state captured from the Let’s Worm specimen.

productProof.title: Editorial character without fragile layouts
productProof.description: Paper, ink, mauve, Caslon, Futura, and the worm motif adapt across themes while stories, bylines, summaries, and navigation remain structurally clear.

image.alt: Let’s Worm story page showing editorial typography, contributor credits, issue context, and long-form reading layout

accessibility.title: Native interaction carries the expressive layer
accessibility.description: A three-pixel focus ring, reduced-motion transitions, mobile-menu focus containment, forced-colors fallback, and responsive reflow protect the reading experience.

internalNotes: The collaboration contains more than 100 works, but the current site is a curated selection rather than a full archive migration. Dan leads the writing and defined most editorial categories; Pete illustrates, occasionally edits or offers opinions, and designed and built the current site. No audience metrics are currently available.
